java_locations.role: Scans Display source before row construction, enters raw mode for `[[...]]`, `<math>...</math>`, and `<latex>...</latex>`, and interprets escaped newline controls only outside raw mode.
Consumes the complete raw `[[...]]` token and retains literal backslash-n bytes in URL and tooltip fields.
Recognizes the complete raw URL token before ordinary Creole text processing.

rust_locations.role: Already models Java Display raw mode correctly for state transition labels.
Splits literal backslash-n before Creole/link parsing, truncating URLs and rendering their suffix as ordinary text.
Splits class member source on every literal backslash-n before a complete raw link token reaches the renderer.
Repeats the unconditional split while measuring and emitting class Display content.

claimed_invariant: Escaped Display newline controls create rows only outside raw Creole URL, math, and LaTeX blocks. Raw block bytes reach their domain parser intact. In particular, a literal backslash-n inside a URL remains in href and is normalized only when producing the SVG title.
causal_divergence: Rust has a correct raw-mode scanner only in the state transition model. Sequence measurement/emission and class member parsing/rendering independently split on every literal backslash-n first. The shared Creole parser therefore receives a truncated `[[...]]` token in those families, even though its direct unit path handles the complete token correctly.
planned_model_change: Extract a parser-level raw-aware Display newline splitter from the existing state model. Use it in sequence Display row measurement/emission and class body/member row expansion. Keep the raw token unchanged; hyperlink parsing and title normalization remain separate downstream responsibilities. Add parser, sequence, and class tests with renamed labels and controls both inside and outside raw blocks.
perturbation_axes: sequence message labels versus class member labels
literal backslash-n inside a URL versus outside a raw block
implicit URL tooltip versus explicit brace tooltip
URL raw blocks versus math and LaTeX raw blocks
single versus multiple linked and unlinked Creole runs
acceptance: Both known generic-creole counterexamples preserve URL bytes and pass the no-oracle structural comparator.
Fresh held-out inputs verify raw-block protection and ordinary escaped-newline splitting on independent axes.
Parser and renderer library suites pass.
An independent checker records a verdict at the exact implementation revision.
